questions.question: In ancient times, what shape was Earth once thought to be, and how were the stars and Sun believed to move?
options: Earth was thought to be flat, with all the stars and the Sun moving around it.
Earth was thought to be a sphere that remained stationary while stars moved in straight lines.
Earth was thought to be a cylinder, with the Sun and stars fixed in place.
Earth was thought to be flat, with only the Moon moving around it while the Sun was stationary.

questions.question: Until which century did most people believe that the Earth was situated at the centre of the universe?
options: The 12th century
The 14th century
The 16th century
The 18th century

questions.question: What is the angle of tilt of the axis on which the Earth spins?
options: 12.5 degrees
23.5 degrees
45.0 degrees
90.0 degrees

questions.question: In which direction does the gravitational force of a planet, moon, or star pull nearby objects?
options: Away from the surface into deep space
Towards the centre of the large object
In a circular path parallel to the object's surface
Towards the magnetic north pole of the object

questions.question: How does the mass of an object affect the strength of its gravitational pull?
options: The greater the mass, the weaker its gravity.
The greater the mass, the stronger its gravity.
Mass has no effect on the strength of gravity.
Only objects with low mass have a gravitational pull.

questions.question: What role does Earth's gravity play in the motion of the Moon?
options: It pushes the Moon away, preventing it from colliding with Earth.
It pulls the Moon towards the centre of Earth, changing its direction and causing it to orbit.
It stops the Moon from spinning on its own axis.
It heats the Moon's surface by pulling its atmosphere closer.

questions.question: What happens to rays of light when they hit a surface face-on compared to when they hit at an angle?
options: They are completely absorbed and do not reflect.
They are more spread out over a larger area.
They are less spread out than if they hit at an angle.
They bend at a ninety-degree angle upon impact.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a planet?
options: A small fragment of ice that floats randomly in deep space.
A very large sphere of rock or gas that orbits a star.
A giant burning ball of hot gas that emits its own light.
A collection of billions of stars held together by gravity.

questions.question: How do the distances between objects in our solar system compare to the actual physical sizes of the objects themselves?
options: The distances are very small, meaning objects are almost touching.
The distances are roughly equal to the diameters of the objects.
The distances are very, very large compared to the sizes of the objects.
The distances are constantly fluctuating between extremely close and extremely far.

questions.question: Why do countries located near the Equator not experience distinct summer and winter seasons?
options: Because they are much closer to the Sun than the polar regions all year.
Because they stay close to 'face-on' to the Sun all year round.
Because they spin at a much faster rate than the rest of the Earth.
Because they are shielded from solar radiation by thick cloud cover.

questions.question: Why do the stars in the night sky look so much smaller and dimmer than our Sun?
options: Because they are much younger and have not reached full brightness.
Because they are made of different, colder types of gases.
Because they are much further away from us.
Because Earth's atmosphere blocks most of their light.

questions.question: What is a light-year, and why is it used by astronomers?
options: It is the time it takes for Earth to orbit the Sun, used to measure planetary ages.
It is the distance light travels in one year, making it suitable for measuring vast distances in space.
It is the speed at which light travels through a vacuum, used to measure the brightness of stars.
It is the distance from the Earth to the Sun, used to measure local solar system distances.

questions.question: What is a galaxy in the universe?
options: A solar system containing exactly eight planets and one central star.
A group in the universe containing billions of stars.
A cloud of dust and gas where new planets are formed.
A single massive star surrounded by orbiting comets.

questions.question: How long does it take for Earth to complete one full orbit around the Sun?
options: 24 hours
27.3 days
365.25 days
100 days

questions.question: What is the shape of Earth's orbit around the Sun?
options: An extremely elongated, narrow oval
A perfect square with rounded corners
An almost perfect circle
A completely irregular spiral
